summary: CRSHMARKET launched Rip It Packs (Pokémon, One Piece, baseball; vault, trade or ship), and it was the loudest new digital-pack story of the day. GameStop Power Packs stayed in the news with a post saying GameStop bought a $250K 1st Edition Neo Destiny Gengar PSA 10 for pack inventory. Collector Crypt's $CARDS got an Upbit listing story plus more Coinbase-roadmap and PayBox talk. Solflare Packs stayed steady and positive: first-time rips and late-night opens from community accounts. Mainstream collectors still hit the same walls — empty shelves, resealed product, and how to spot fake PSA slabs — while a small rival (JustPlayTCG) openly pitched Apple Pay and Google Pay for graded packs.

sources_note: X search via the x connector, posts from 2026-11-04 09:00 UTC to 2026-11-05 09:10 UTC. 8 post searches and 1 X news search. Engagement numbers are copied from the X API at scan time; post texts are trimmed. Phygitals $8.36M and Collector Crypt revenue claims are from unverified third-party posts. The GameStop $250K Gengar buy is a hobby account's claim (marked #AD for Power Packs). Upbit $CARDS listing, Walmart drawings, Delta Reign and Mudwater items are X news summaries. Payments talk was thin beyond JustPlayTCG pitching Apple Pay/Google Pay for graded packs; most other Apple Pay hits were scam/carding spam and were skipped. Skipped: Rips by Triumph referral spam, HaloArena sold-out reply farms, $CARDS token shills without pack product context, UNCOVER store promo repeats, and packspy money-multiplier framing. Creators already in the skip list were left out of new_creators. Ryanhlx was in yesterday's new_creators and was left out of today's list.
